messages:
mira: Heads-up — Acme (acme-prod) just escalated: lots of 401s and big egress to ap-southeast-1 after last failover policy change. Customer says requests that should hit us-west-2 are landing in ap-southeast-1. Repro steps and logs below.

acme-prod: Repro (from their env):
1) curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Region: us-west-2' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}'
-> 401, latency 2.1s, response headers: x-region-served: ap-southeast-1, x-request-id: req-20260223-abcd
We made ~12k calls in last 3h; egress bill spiked ~USD 3.6k.

sam: Can you paste the exact request-id(s) and a sample full response (headers + body)? also which API key/org id?

acme-prod: One sample req: req-20260223-abcd. Org: acme-corp. We'll DM the token details to support channel.

kevin: Thanks. Preliminary guess: failover priority order may be reversed or weights mis-parsed, plus sticky routing TTL issue. Any recent policy commits?

mira: Customer policy (copied from Console export):
```
{
  "failover_policy": {
    "priority": ["ap-southeast-1","eu-west-1","us-west-2"],
    "weights": [70,20,10],
    "sticky": true,
    "sticky_ttl_sec": 0
  }
}
```
They say intended primary is us-west-2.

kevin: That config explains it — priority array lists ap-southeast first. If frontend or API reversed order on save we may have shipped reversed arrays. Sticky TTL 0 means sessions are essentially immortal in some code paths? bad.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-policy-service v3.2.1 rolled to prod at 2490001100 by @deploy-bot

ingrid: Investigating DB. Found saved policy for acme-corp where priority array is reversed compared to UI intent. Root cause: UI toggling reorder bug where we serialize list with push/pop causing reversed net order. Also weight parser rounded floats down and trimmed decimals; a decimal weight of 0.6 became 0 and triggered fallback. Sticky TTL 0 caused immediate re-evaluation and some requests bounced to fallback region, generating auth churn.

alex: Immediate mitigation: 1) pin customer's key to us-west-2 via console override (we can do this for them temporarily). 2) update their failover_policy in DB to correct ordering and set sticky_ttl_sec to 3600. 3) flush router sticky entries for that org (endpoint: POST /internal/routing/flush?org=acme-corp). Will coordinate SRE.

billing-bot: Noted — creating ticket to evaluate egress credit for acme-corp. Ticket #BILL-783.

sam: Can SRE confirm flush step & provide confirmation once done? Also open a PR to fix UI serialization edge-case.

ingrid: Flush done at 2490001250 — routers returned 200. Verified subsequent requests from Acme show x-region-served: us-west-2 and no 401s in the next 5 minutes of smoke tests. I also pushed a temporary DB change to reorder priority for acme-corp.

kevin: Repro steps (for eng):
1) Set failover_policy.priority = ["ap-southeast-1","eu-west-1","us-west-2"] in Console and save.
2) Observe saved JSON via API GET /v1/orgs/acme-corp/config -> priority reversed from intended in many cases.
3) Make request with header `X-Region: us-west-2` and see header `x-region-served: ap-southeast-1`.
Sample failing response snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-region-served: ap-southeast-1
x-request-id: req-20260223-abcd
{
  "error": "token invalid"
}
```

mira: Customer accepted temporary pin + flush. Next actions: SRE postmortem, frontend hotfix PR (assign to @sam), console hotfix to validate priority order, tests to catch weight decimal parsing, and billing follow-up for credit. I'll own follow-up items.

alex: I'll contact acme point-of-contact and confirm credit/tracking.

kevin: PR submitted for UI serialization fix: https://git.internal/redwood/frontend/pull/4321 (small WIP).

acme-prod: Confirmed after pin+flush: requests now served from us-west-2, 401s gone. Thanks for the quick follow-up.

mira: Closing on this thread — will post postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
